s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with headache and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Large lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
key_facts: 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
Headache exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
Bilateral past-pointing on neurologic examination
Intention tremor on neurologic examination
6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
Mass extends craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
Involvement and expansion of Meckel’s cave
Small extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
Multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
Interspersed enhancing septa and T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
Curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
Anterior displacement of the cavernous sinus
Encasement with mild narrowing of the left petrous internal carotid artery

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated mass at cerebellopontine angle with cystic and solid components

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Dural involvement and compression of adjacent structures

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of Meckel's cave and extension into infratemporal fossa

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Midline location and involvement of clivus

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Multiloculated cystic areas with partial suppression on T2-FLAIR imaging

raw.rationale: The tumor's location centered at the left cerebellopontine angle, involvement and expansion of Meckel's cave, and extension into the infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma, which typically arises from the trigeminal nerve and can have a complex, lobulated appearance with cystic and solid components.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically centered at the internal auditory canal, which is not the primary location of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Often has a more homogeneous appearance and may have a dural tail sign, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Typically centered at the clivus and often has a more aggressive appearance with bone destruction, which is not the primary feature of this mass.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Typically has a more uniform, cystic appearance with restricted diffusion on MRI, which is not consistent with the complex, solid, and cystic components of this mass.
